clue.text: Some deplore Saul's character in the Bible

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dim view of the conduct of King Saul in the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits at the join of 'deplorE SAUl's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob's twin brother, who sold his birthright, is a figure from the Book of Genesis.

clue.text: He's era's peak when it comes to play

definitions.text: He's era's peak when it comes to play

indicators.note: the letters are set to play, moving freely into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Praise for the greatest dramatist of his age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it comes to play' rearranges HESERASPEAK; the whole clue also describes the Elizabethan playwright, the high point of his era in drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bard is widely called the summit of Elizabethan drama, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Insufficiently promote European articles — the French upped and left

parts.note: un is an indefinite article in French
der is a definite article in German

indicators.note: in a down clue, upped means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: les is French for 'the' in the plural

explanation.surface: A complaint that Europe's grammar words got little publicity once the French walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped' turns LES into SEL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To undersell something is to promote or value it less than it deserves.

clue.text: Lower number of persons departs university after time without work

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the other pieces go round the word for work

parts.note: dep. is the timetable abbreviation for departs
late means after the appointed time
op. is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone leaves college once it is late, having no job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: the other pieces surround the work, which sits just after the departure abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To depopulate a place is to reduce how many people live there.

clue.text: Many with CID trained with force

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: Lots of detectives from the Criminal Investigation Department are put through training together with the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges MANYCID; CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dynamic is full of energy and power, acting forcefully.

clue.text: Plant extra irises for novel result

definitions.meaning: flags are wild irises, so this means set additional ones in the ground

explanation.surface: A gardener sets out more irises and gets a book out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag is another name for the yellow iris; the phrase is also the title of an Evelyn Waugh novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh's wartime satire bears this title, and flags are irises you could set in the ground.

clue.text: Criticise fantastic answer offering a universal solution

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
ace is slang for excellent or fantastic

explanation.surface: Someone slates a brilliant reply that claims to fix everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all remedy for every problem, the idea of one fix for all ills.

clue.text: Winged messenger initially warning danger

parts.note: alar is an adjective meaning relating to wings

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word messenger

explanation.surface: A winged herald arrives first to warn of peril.
explanation.walkthrough: ALAR is a rare word meaning of or like wings.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal that warns people of danger.

clue.text: One carrying off temple sections as river rose, gallons pouring in

indicators.note: gallons pouring into the river means its letter goes inside
in a down clue, rose means the river's name reads upward

parts.note: the Nile is Africa's great river

explanation.surface: A thief makes off with bits of a temple while the river floods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' turns NILE into ELIN, and 'pouring in' puts G inside it. Lord Elgin took sculptures from the Parthenon in Athens to Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Elgin removed the Parthenon marbles from the Athens temple, so he carried off its sections.

clue.text: A figure child might want for Play Station

definitions.text: A figure child might want for Play
definitions.meaning: a toy bear named after the station, from the children's books

explanation.surface: A child wants a toy for a games console.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play Station' looks like the games console, but splits into two senses: a teddy bear from the children's books and a London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmalade-loving bear from Michael Bond's books shares his name with a London terminus.

clue.text: Report drug, but not heroin

indicators.note: but not means the following item is dropped from the drug's name

parts.note: bhang is cannabis as used in India
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Inform on a drug dealer, though the drug isn't heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud explosive noise, as of a gun, which is a bang.

clue.text: Famous horse Queen's used at opening of Edinburgh tattoo

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: opening of picks the first letter of the word Edinburgh

parts.note: a tattoo is a drumbeat

explanation.surface: The monarch's horse appears at the start of the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Rum won Britain's Grand National steeplechase three times in the 1970s; the surface's Edinburgh tattoo is the military show there.
explanation.definitionFit: The racehorse that won the Grand National three times is the most celebrated jumper in British racing.

clue.text: Rare company getting millions for unit in merger

indicators.note: for means one piece takes the place of another in the merger word

parts.note: a union is a merging of two bodies
I is the Roman numeral for one, a unit
M is millions, so MM is millions in the plural

explanation.surface: In a corporate merger, a scarce firm is swapped for millions in place of a unit.
explanation.walkthrough: COMM replaces the I of UNION to make UN-COMM-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon is seldom found, which is what rare means.

clue.text: Veto hormone designed to make one euphoric

indicators.note: designed means the letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A banned hormone has been engineered as a mood-lifting drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges VETOHORMONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be over the moon is an idiom for being delighted, elated.

clue.text: Primate holds saint to be a feature of the eastern church

indicators.note: holds means the primate's word goes round the other piece

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey clutches a holy figure, a sight in an Orthodox church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern church' sounds like the Orthodox Church, but means the east end of a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the vaulted recess, usually at the east end of a church building.

clue.text: MOD men race to get out requisition

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Defence Ministry staff hurry to evacuate and seize a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MODMENRACE; the MOD is Britain's Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: To commandeer is to seize property for official, often military, use.

clue.text: English writer's study into origins of Doctor Thorne needing support

indicators.note: into means the earlier pieces go inside the outer letters
origins of takes the first letter of each of the two words Doctor and Thorne

parts.note: a pen is a writer's instrument
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: An English author's study of Trollope's novel Doctor Thorne is in need of backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Thorne is a novel by Anthony Trollope; 'into' places the writer-and-study pieces between its initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dependent relies on another for help and support.

clue.text: One could cut down sources of this sweetener

definitions.text: One could cut down sources of this sweetener

parts.words: One could cut down sources of this sweetener
parts.note: the sources are trees, so a lumberjack fells the trees whose sap gives a pancake topping

explanation.surface: Someone could reduce the supply of a sugar substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down sources' reads as reducing supplies, but means felling the trees that give the sap.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet syrup comes from the sap of trees that could be felled.

clue.text: Poles introduced to track event supporter

indicators.note: introduced to means the poles go into the track word

parts.note: spoor is the track or trail of an animal
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Polish athletes appear at a race meeting with a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests Polish people, but means the North and South poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor backs an event, often by paying for it.

clue.text: Try to get something from family? It a Halloween tradition

parts.note: to pump someone is to try to extract information from them
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Interrogating your relatives at the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Carving a hollow gourd into a lantern is a Halloween custom.

clue.text: Shame mine's unknown

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Disgrace that a colliery is unidentified.
explanation.definitionFit: A shame in the sense of a regrettable thing, as in 'what a pity'.

clue.text: Sort of tamale which is baked in a tin?

indicators.note: sort means the letters are sorted into a different order

explanation.surface: A tamale variety that is cooked in a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' rearranges OFTAMALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The minced-meat dish is baked in a loaf tin, so it is something cooked in a tin.

clue.text: Doctor denied I should consume old red wine

indicators.note: consume means the remaining letters take in the old piece
denied means the letter I is refused, dropped

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor forbids a patient from drinking aged claret.
explanation.walkthrough: MEDIC minus I gives MEDC, which takes O inside. Médoc is a Bordeaux wine region.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux wine from the region of that name.

clue.text: Left in a bad place for photos

indicators.note: in means the left piece goes inside the other letters

parts.note: bum is slang for bad, as in a bum deal

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in a grim spot for a snapshot.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a book in which photographs are kept.

clue.text: 500 or 1000 in cash

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, '500 or 1000 in cash', fits MONKEY only for 500; slang gives no 1000, and with no usable scan or blog the true clue cannot be confirmed

clue.text: What's due to be endlessly discussed when leaders are retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read in reverse order
leaders are the first letters of the four words before 'when'

explanation.surface: Something owed is debated forever once the bosses step down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes TBED from 'to be endlessly discussed', and 'are retiring' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money owed, something that is due to be paid.

clue.text: Polar explorer has to limit weight

parts.note: to shackle is to restrict or limit
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: An Antarctic adventurer has to keep his load down.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Shackleton led expeditions to Antarctica.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Ernest Shackleton led several British expeditions to the Antarctic.

clue.text: In contrast, happen to be short, working capital being invested

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, so the capital goes into the other pieces
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to come about is to happen
on means working, as a machine that is on
Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: A finance clause about putting working capital into a short-term investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last letter of the verb, and 'being invested' places the city inside. 'capital' reads as money in the surface but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparison weighs things against each other, which is to set them in contrast.

clue.text: One crazy about eastern melody

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A madman obsessed with the East hums a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NUT into TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune is a melody, a sequence of musical notes.
